rows.label: Levied by
rows.value: About 6,000 local government units: municipalities, townships, counties, school districts, park districts and other taxing districts
rows.note: The state itself does not levy property tax.

rows.label: State oversight
rows.value: Illinois Department of Revenue (equalization factors, sales ratio studies, assessor education)
rows.note: IDOR does not administer property tax; counties and taxing districts do. IDOR sets equalization factors and trains assessment officials.

source.title: Illinois Department of Revenue: Property Tax (Local Governments)

rows.label: Levy growth limit (PTELL)
rows.value: Lesser of 5% or the prior year's CPI increase, for taxing districts in counties under the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law
rows.note: Applies in Cook, the collar counties and counties that adopted it by referendum; voters can approve higher increases. Home-rule units are not covered.

source.title: Illinois Department of Revenue: PIO-62 An Overview of the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law

rows.label: General homestead exemption (maximum)
rows.value: Up to $6,000 of equalized assessed value in most counties; $8,000 in counties next to Cook; $10,000 in Cook County
rows.note: Equals the increase in the home's EAV above its 1977 EAV, capped at these amounts (35 ILCS 200/15-175).

sections.title: Illinois sales and use tax

rows.label: State sales tax rate
rows.note: Retailers' occupation tax and use tax: State rate on general merchandise (the "high rate").

source.title: PIO-115, Tax Rate Information for Retail Sales of Food and Medicine

rows.label: Local sales taxes
rows.value: Counties, municipalities, mass-transit and other districts add local retailers' occupation taxes to the State rate; from 2026 municipalities and counties may also impose a 1% local grocery tax
rows.note: IDOR's Tax Rate Finder (MyTax Illinois) gives the combined rate by location.

source.title: Sales & Use Taxes

rows.label: Groceries (food for home consumption)
rows.note: The State's 1% tax on groceries (qualifying food) ended on 1 January 2026; municipalities and counties may impose a local grocery tax of exactly 1%. Soft drinks, candy, alcohol and food prepared for immediate consumption stay at the 6.25% rate.

source.title: Informational Bulletin FY 2026-03, Illinois Grocery Tax Changes Effective January 1, 2026

rows.label: Prescription drugs
rows.note: Qualifying drugs and medical appliances (prescription and some nonprescription medicines) stay at the State's 1% rate.

source.title: Informational Bulletin FY 2026-03, Illinois Grocery Tax Changes Effective January 1, 2026

rows.label: Use tax rate
rows.note: Taxable purchases on which no sales tax was paid (storage, use or consumption in the state). The Use Tax Act tax complements the retailers' occupation tax at the same State rates (6.25% general, 1% qualifying drugs).

source.title: Sales & Use Taxes

rows.label: Remote sellers: sales threshold
rows.note: Remote retailer's cumulative gross receipts from sales to Illinois purchasers in the preceding 12 months (checked quarterly): must collect at $100,000 or more. Either threshold triggers the obligation.

source.title: Sales & Use Taxes

rows.label: Remote sellers: transactions threshold
rows.note: Remote retailer's separate sales transactions to Illinois purchasers in the preceding 12 months (checked quarterly). Counted in transactions. Either threshold triggers the obligation.

sections.title: Illinois estate and inheritance taxes

rows.label: Estate tax: exemption
rows.note: Exclusion amount: a taxable threshold, not a credit; Form 700 is filed when the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts exceeds it. The tax is figured with an interrelated calculation (the Attorney General's calculator).

sections.note: Taxes the state levies on estates of decedents and on heirs, in addition to the federal estate tax (national page). Each row has its own official source.
